: 
This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH-5 2

. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 02.09.2022 at about 9.45 a.m. petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-L-4737 near Dasanapura, Opp.
TATA Dream Motors, Tumkur - Bengaluru NH-48 Service Road, Bengaluru, at that time, Tata 1109 bearing Reg.No.KA-35-B-1600 being driven by its driver came at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against motor cycle on which petitioner was moving as a result, she fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, she was shifted V.P.Magnus Hospital, wherein she took treatment as inpatient, towards the medical expenses she has sent an amount of Rs.1,00,000/-.

3. At the time of the accident she was aged about 48 years, hale and healthy, doing milk business,
thereby SCCH-5 earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. due to the accidental injuries, till today she is taking treatment as outdoor patient.
Out of this accident crime No.376/2020 is registered against the driver of the said Tata 1109 before the Nelamangala Traffic Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is the insurer, respondent No.2 is owner of the said offending vehicle, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- with interest.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.
He has denied involvement of Tata 1109 vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-35-B-1600 in the alleged accident.
Further submitted that, petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary and proper parties for the SCCH-5 adjudication of the case.

Further denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner, occurrence of the accident and admits issuance of insurance policy in respect of the said Tata vehicle and the same was valid since 04.01.2022 to 03.01.2023, if there is any liability, it is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Respondent No.1 is liable to take shelter under Sec.147 and 149 of M.V.Act.

There is no compliance of Sec.134(c)
and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle does not possess valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: Respondent No.2/owner has appeared and filed written statement, wherein admitted ownership over the Tata 1109 bearing Reg.No.KA-35-B-1600 having SCCH-5 insured with respondent No.1 vide policy No.2315203217786502000 valid from 04.04.2022 to 03.01.2023 and denied entire averments of the petition.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

6. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 02.09.2022 at about 9.45 a.m. when petitioner was a pillion rider on motor Scooter bearing Reg.No. KA-52- L-4737 near Dasanapura, Opp. Tata Dreams Motors, Tumkur- Bengaluru, NH-48 Service Road,
Bengaluru at that time, Tata 1109 bearing Reg.No.KA-35- B-1600 driven by its rider in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the petitioner and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
SCCH-5 2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
7. In order to prove his case, Petitioner herself deposed her evidence as PW-1, examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW-2 and marked 13 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and closed her evidence.
On the other hand, there is no evidence of respondents.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
SCCH-5 ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove her case, petitioner has deposed her evidence as PW-1, in her chief-examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in her petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of hand sketch is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.6.

sentences.text: Further to substantiate the petitioner case, she examined one Doctor as PW-2.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 and his records those have marked i.e., as FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, hand sketch, IMV SCCH-5 Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 02.09.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
11.

Per contra, except appearance, filing of written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 02.09.2022 at about 9.45 a.m. while she was proceeding as pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-L-4737near Dasanapura, Opp.
Tata Dream Motors, Tumkur - Bengaluru NH-48 Service Road, Bengaluru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the SCCH-5 arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
12. On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the Tata 1109 driver.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in he favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-

As per the evidence of the petitioner, she had sustained posttraumatic right foot degloving on the dorsum of the great toe, metatarsal comminuted fracture of the middle phalanx with extensor tendon injury, for which she has undergone surgery with wound debridement and K-wire fixation.

In this regard SCCH-5 she has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.7, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8 issued by VP Magnus Hospital, wherein she took treatment as indoor patient since 02.09.2022 to 05.09.2022.

Further she has furnished medical bills for Rs.36,323/- marked as Ex.P.10 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.11.
14.
Ofcourse, PW-2 Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS is examined as PW-2.

To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited clinical notes marked as Ex.P.12 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.13 and he has assessed physical disability of the right lower limb at the rate of 24% and whole body physical disability at the rate of 8%.
In cross-examination he has categorically admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner and he has not seen the old X-ray Films and case sheet.
Further deposed that petitioner had sustained right foot degloving SCCH-5 injury with extensor tendon injury and all the injuries are healed and K-wire is removed and now fractures are united.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 8% for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

15. As per the case of the petitioner, she was aged about 48 years, for proof of her age, she has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.9, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner is 12.09.1975 and the alleged accident is occurred on 02.09.2022, accordingly relying on Girijamma vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176546519/
4

sentences.text: 16. As per her case, she was doing milk vending business, thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m., to prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.14,750/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is admitted fact that, as per the discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8, petitioner was admitted in VP Magnus Hospital as inpatient from 02.09.2022 to 05.09.2022 i.e., for 3 days.

For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income as per the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.14,750/- p.m.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said quantum for the period she was admitted as inpatient in the hospital.
So petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,475/- towards loss on income during laid up period.
18. Further admittedly she has exhibited Ex.P.10 medical bills for Rs.36,323/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is considered.

Further on perusal of Ex.P.7 SCCH-5 wound certificate reveals that, petitioner had sustained CLW over the right foot, degloving left foot with communited fracture of 1st metatorsal, CLW over the left foot and over left knee joint, abrasion and swelling over left forearm, which is grievous injuries out of the accident caused on 02.09.2022.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Rajashekar C. for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.36,323/-.
19.
Except denial in the written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to step into SCCH-5 witness box nor to prove the allegations as alleged in the written statement.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondents have filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case, because it is bounden duty of him to prove the defence as taken in the written statement.
Except filing of the written statement, cross-examining the PW-1 and PW-2 orally, have not taken any steps to disprove the case of the petitioner.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical bills and other compensation as stated below.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,66,878/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

22. In the case on hand, respondent No.1 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.2315 2032 1778 6502 000 which is valid for the period from 04.01.2022 to 03.01.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 02.09.2022 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of R2 shall go against R1, so that, R1/insurer is SCCH-5 directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: : 
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,66,878/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Sixty Six Thousand Eight Hundred Seventy Eight Only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to her SCCH-5 account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in her name.
